todays_goal: Advance from one-step equations to Grade 6 inequalities and number-line representations.

lessons.subject: mathematics
lessons.previous_learning: Day 20 one-step equations were very strong. The only remaining issue was describing a check too vaguely rather than explicitly substituting into the original equation.
lessons.course_context: Brief equation-check retrieval, then move to inequalities as sets of possible solutions.
learning_objectives: Graph inequalities on a number line.
Use open versus closed circles appropriately.
Test whether a value is a solution.
lessons.why_it_matters: Inequalities model real limits, minimums, maximums, and ranges instead of one exact answer.

vocabulary.definition: a comparison showing that quantities may not be equal
all values that make an inequality true
the boundary value shown on the number line

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: an equation often has a specific solution. An inequality can have many solutions. Use an open circle when the endpoint is not included and a closed circle when it is included.

worked_examples.title: x > 5
worked_examples.explanation: 5 itself is not included; greater values lie to the right.

worked_examples.title: At least
worked_examples.problem: Rider must be at least 48 inches tall.

independent_practice.prompt: Write an inequality for at least 52 inches tall.
Write an inequality for no more than $30.
A roster can have at most 18 players. Write an inequality.

exit_ticket.prompt: What is the difference between an equation and an inequality?
exit_ticket.answer: An equation states equality; an inequality compares quantities and can have a set of solutions.

exit_ticket.prompt: Write an inequality for 'You need more than 20 points.'
Is 20 a solution to p > 20? Explain.
exit_ticket.answer: No, because 20 is not greater than 20.

lessons.voice_prompt: Start with a 3-minute retrieval: a real check means substitute the solution into the original equation. Then teach inequalities using the whiteboard number line. Ask whether the endpoint is included before choosing open or closed circle. Use different values from assigned problems and never draw the assigned final graph.
lessons.teacher_notes: Grade 6 progression; do not jump to multi-step inequality solving.
